note: Known Salesforce deployment error patterns. Each entry is a hint for the agent, not a verdict: 'pattern' is a case-insensitive regular expression matched against the problem text, 'refs' names the capture groups that hold a referenced component.

categories.missing-dependency: The deployment references a component that the target org does not have and that is not part of this deployment.
categories.code: The source itself is wrong: it does not compile or contradicts another component in the same deployment.
categories.test-failure: An Apex test ran and failed.
categories.coverage: The tests passed, but the coverage requirement is not met.
categories.org-state: The target org is in a state that blocks the change: data, active versions, references, features or licenses.
categories.permissions: The deploying user or the org lacks a permission, license or feature.
categories.environment: The failure is not about the metadata: authentication, network, timeout, platform availability.

patterns.title: A query uses a field the target org does not have
patterns.advice: Check whether the field exists in the repository. If it does, it is missing from this deployment (delta too narrow, wrong manifest, .forceignore) or the deploying user cannot see it (field-level security). If it does not, it only exists in another org or the name is misspelled.

patterns.title: Apex uses a custom field the target org does not have
patterns.advice: Usually a follow-up error of a missing field. Fix the missing field first and re-validate.

patterns.title: Apex uses a variable, property or field that does not exist
patterns.advice: A plain compile error if the name is local to the class. If it names a property of another class or a field, that class or field is older in the org than in the source, or is missing from this deployment.

patterns.pattern: Unable to find Apex action class referenced as '([^']+)'
patterns.title: A Lightning component imports an Apex class the target org does not have
patterns.advice: Deploy the class together with the component, or correct the class name in the `@salesforce/apex/...` import. An org does not report all broken imports at once, so more may follow after this one is fixed.

patterns.pattern: Unable to find Apex action method referenced as '([^'.]+)\.([^']+)'
patterns.title: A Lightning component imports an Apex method that is missing or not @AuraEnabled
patterns.advice: The class exists, the method does not, or it lacks `@AuraEnabled`. Check the method name in the import and the annotation in the class. If the source is right, the org holds an older version of the class that is not part of this deployment.

patterns.title: A Lightning component uses another component that is not in the org
patterns.advice: The component is used as a tag in the template or imported as `c/name`. Deploy it in the same deployment or correct the name; a tag `<c-my-card>` refers to the bundle `myCard`.

patterns.title: A Lightning component imports a message channel the org does not have
patterns.advice: Add the message channel to the deployment or correct the name in the `@salesforce/messageChannel/...` import.

patterns.pattern: Invalid reference (\S+) of type sobject[A-Za-z]* in file (\S+)
patterns.title: A Lightning component imports a field or object the org does not have
patterns.advice: The `@salesforce/schema/...` import names a field or object that is missing in the target org or hidden from the deploying user. Deploy it together with the component or correct the name.

patterns.pattern: Invalid reference (\S+) of type ([A-Za-z]+) in file (\S+)
patterns.title: A Lightning component imports something the org does not have
patterns.advice: The type names what is missing: `label` (a custom label), `resourceUrl` (a static resource), `customPermission`, `contentAssetUrl`. Add it to the deployment or correct the name in the import.

patterns.title: A Lightning web component does not compile
patterns.advice: A plain error in the JavaScript or the template at the given line and column. It would fail in every org; the local linter or `sf lightning dev` shows the same error before a deployment.

patterns.title: A component sits in a folder the target org does not have
patterns.advice: Email templates, reports, dashboards and documents live in folders that are metadata of their own. Deploy the folder in the same deployment or before it. Every component of that folder fails with this message, so one missing folder produces many failures.

patterns.title: A component refers to an email template the target org does not have
patterns.advice: Usually a follow-up error: the template itself failed in the same deployment, often because its folder is missing. Fix the template first.

patterns.pattern: Could not resolve list view column: ([A-Za-z0-9_.]+)
patterns.title: A list view shows a field the target org does not have
patterns.advice: Deploy the field with the list view, or remove the column. Standard fields that exist only with a feature or in a newer release give the same message.

patterns.title: A component refers to another component that is not in the org
patterns.advice: Add the referenced component to the deployment, or remove the reference. Typical for permission sets, profiles and layouts that still list fields, classes or record types that were deleted or never deployed.

patterns.pattern: (?:referenceTo value of '([^']+)' does not resolve to a valid sObject type|Invalid type: ([A-Za-z0-9_]+)|sObject type '([^']+)' is not supported)
patterns.title: An object or type is unknown in the target org
patterns.advice: Deploy the object or class first or in the same deployment. If it belongs to a managed package or a feature (Person Accounts, Field Service, Quotes), install the package or enable the feature in the target org.

patterns.pattern: An object '([^']+)' of type ([A-Za-z]+) was named in package\.xml, but was not found in zipped directory
patterns.title: The manifest names a component that is not in the source
patterns.advice: Remove the entry from the manifest or restore the file. Often a renamed or deleted file whose manifest entry stayed.

patterns.pattern: Method does not exist or incorrect signature: (.+?)(?: \(|$)
patterns.title: Apex calls a method that does not exist with that signature
patterns.advice: The caller and the called class are out of sync. Check whether the called class is part of this deployment and whether the org holds an older version of it.

patterns.title: Apex uses a type the target org does not expose
patterns.advice: The type belongs to a feature, a license or an API version the org does not have, or to a managed package class that is not global. Enable the feature in the target org, raise the API version of the class, or remove the dependency for this org.

patterns.pattern: Dependent class is invalid and needs recompilation
patterns.title: A class depends on another class that does not compile
patterns.advice: Follow-up error. Find the first class that fails for its own reason and fix that one.

patterns.pattern: is forceignored but is required for
patterns.title: A file a component needs is excluded by .forceignore
patterns.advice: A rule in `.forceignore` matches the metadata file of a component whose other files are deployed. Narrow the rule or ignore the whole component.

patterns.title: A metadata file is not well-formed XML
patterns.advice: The named file cannot be parsed, typically after a merge conflict was resolved by hand: leftover conflict markers, a tag closed twice or not at all. It fails before anything reaches the org.

patterns.pattern: (?:Unexpected token|Missing '[^']+' at|Illegal assignment from|Unexpected file found in package directory)
patterns.title: The source does not compile
patterns.advice: A plain code error in the named file and line. It would fail in every org.

patterns.pattern: This class name's value is invalid: ([A-Za-z0-9_]+)
patterns.title: A test class named for the run does not exist in the org
patterns.advice: The test level names a class the target org does not have, or one without test methods. Check the spelling and whether the class is part of this deployment; a list of tests kept in the workflow goes stale when a class is renamed or deleted.

patterns.title: A test assertion failed
patterns.advice: The behaviour differs from what the test expects. Decide whether the change or the test is wrong. Do not weaken the assertion to get a green run.

patterns.title: Test data misses a required field
patterns.advice: Either the test builds an incomplete record, or the target org requires a field the source org does not (a required custom field, a different page layout does not matter, but a required field definition does). Compare the field definition between repository and org.

patterns.title: A validation rule rejects the test data
patterns.advice: A validation rule in the target org blocks the record the test creates. Check whether the rule is in the repository. If it only exists in the org, the org has drifted from the source.

patterns.title: Test data collides with a unique field or a duplicate rule
patterns.advice: The test relies on a value that must be unique, or a duplicate rule is active in the target org. Generate unique values in the test or check the duplicate rules of the org.

patterns.pattern: UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW: unable to obtain exclusive access
patterns.title: The deployment could not lock a record in the org
patterns.advice: Not caused by the change. Something else was writing at the same time: another deployment, a running test execution or a scheduled job. Re-run. If it recurs, look for deployments or test runs that overlap in this org and run them one after the other.

patterns.title: A record was locked by another transaction
patterns.advice: Typically intermittent: parallel test execution or another job touching the same records. Re-run once. If it recurs, disable parallel testing for the affected classes or isolate the shared records.

patterns.title: Setup and non-setup objects are written in one transaction
patterns.advice: Wrap the setup DML (User, PermissionSetAssignment, Group) in System.runAs in the test.

patterns.title: A governor limit was hit
patterns.advice: Something in the transaction grew: a new trigger, flow or loop adds queries or DML. Look at automation added to the object in this change and at flows in the org that are not in the repository.

patterns.title: The platform rejects a value the test writes
patterns.advice: A field holds a value that is not allowed in this org: an inactive or unlicensed owner, a record type or picklist value the org does not have, a lookup to the wrong kind of record. Compare the users, record types and settings the test relies on with the target org.

patterns.pattern: (?:System\.NullPointerException|List has no rows for assignment to SObject)
patterns.title: The test hits missing data
patterns.advice: The code expects a record or value that is not there. Tests that rely on org data (no @TestSetup, SeeAllData=true, custom settings, custom metadata) pass in one org and fail in another.

patterns.pattern: Test coverage of selected Apex (?:Class|Trigger) is (\d+)%, at least (\d+)% test coverage is required
patterns.title: A deployed class is below the coverage requirement
patterns.advice: With RunSpecifiedTests every class and trigger in the deployment needs 75 % from the specified tests alone. Add the test class that covers it to the test list, or extend the tests.

patterns.pattern: Average test coverage across all Apex Classes and Triggers is (\d+)%, at least (\d+)% test coverage is required
patterns.title: Org-wide coverage is below the requirement
patterns.advice: The org as a whole is under 75 %. This is rarely caused by one change; failing tests count as zero coverage, so fix test failures first.

patterns.title: The deploying user lacks access to a referenced record or component
patterns.advice: Check the permissions of the deployment user in the target org (Modify Metadata, Author Apex, access to the referenced record type, queue or user). A referenced user or queue that does not exist in this org gives the same message.

patterns.title: A profile or permission set contains a permission the org does not know
patterns.advice: The permission belongs to a feature or license the target org does not have, or the org is on an older release. Remove the permission from the source or enable the feature.

patterns.title: The org does not allow folders for Lightning email templates
patterns.advice: Enable 'Folders and Enhanced Sharing' for Lightning email templates in the target org (Setup, Lightning Email Templates). Scratch orgs need the matching setting in their definition file. It is an org setting, not something the deployment can switch on.

patterns.pattern: (?:[Nn]ot available for deploy for this organization|is not supported in this organization|requires (?:the )?[A-Za-z ]+ (?:license|feature|permission))
patterns.title: The org lacks a feature or license the metadata needs
patterns.advice: Enable the feature in the target org or exclude the component for this org. Compare the org edition and licenses with the org the metadata was retrieved from.

patterns.title: A package could not be installed in the target org
patterns.advice: The message lists what the org rejected. Typical: the new version removes or changes something the org still uses, or a dependency is missing or older than required. It is about the state of this org, not about the source.

patterns.pattern: (?:This [a-z ]+ is referenced elsewhere in salesforce\.com|Cannot delete|is in use by|is referenced by)
patterns.title: A component cannot be changed or deleted because something still uses it
patterns.advice: Remove the references first (often in the org only: reports, list views, flows versions, layouts), then repeat the destructive change.

patterns.pattern: (?:Cannot change (?:field )?type|Cannot change which object this is a child of|cannot be converted)
patterns.title: A field type change is not allowed with the existing data or references
patterns.advice: Salesforce blocks some type changes through the Metadata API. Change the type in the org manually or migrate through a new field.

patterns.pattern: (?:[Ff]low is already in use|The version of the flow you're updating is active|can't (?:overwrite|delete) an active)
patterns.title: An active flow version blocks the change
patterns.advice: Deploy the flow as a new version or deactivate the active version first. Check the org setting 'Deploy processes and flows as active'.

patterns.pattern: duplicate value found: (.+?) duplicates value on record with id
patterns.title: A component with this name already exists under another id
patterns.advice: The org already has a component with the same developer name, created by hand. Rename or delete the one in the org, or retrieve it into the source.

patterns.pattern: (?:conflicts detected|There are changes in the org that conflict)
patterns.title: Source tracking reports changes in the org
patterns.advice: Someone changed the same components in the org. Retrieve and merge them, or deploy with --ignore-conflicts if the repository is the source of truth.

patterns.pattern: increase --wait timeout to wait for results
patterns.title: The Apex test run did not finish within the wait time
patterns.advice: The tests are still running in the org, or were, when the command gave up, so there is no result to read and the steps that need it fail next. Raise `--wait`, or fetch the result later with `sf apex get test`. A test run that suddenly takes much longer often waits on record locks.

patterns.title: The Salesforce CLI does not start on the Node.js version of the runner
patterns.advice: Not caused by the change. The CLI that was installed needs a newer Node.js than the job provides, so every `sf` command fails before it does anything. Raise the Node.js version in the setup step, or pin the CLI to the version that last worked.

patterns.pattern: (?:Nonexistent flag: (--[A-Za-z-]+)|Exactly one of the following must be provided|Missing required flag|Unexpected arguments?:)
patterns.title: The Salesforce CLI rejects the command line
patterns.advice: The workflow calls the CLI with flags this CLI version does not accept, or leaves out a required one, often because a variable in the command is empty. The command never reached the org; fix the workflow.

patterns.title: An environment variable for a string replacement is not set
patterns.advice: `sfdx-project.json` replaces a placeholder with an environment variable, and the job does not define it. Add the variable or the secret to the step that deploys; a secret that is not available to pull requests from forks gives the same result.

patterns.title: The org has used up its API requests
patterns.advice: Not caused by the change. The org reached its 24-hour API request limit, so the CLI cannot talk to it. Wait, or find what consumes the requests: integrations, frequent pipeline runs, polling.

patterns.title: A step uses an org that was never authenticated in this job
patterns.advice: Usually a follow-up error. The step that logs in or creates the scratch org failed or was skipped earlier in the job, so the alias does not exist; look at the first failed step. If none failed before, the alias in this command differs from the one the login step set.

patterns.pattern: (?:expired access/refresh token|INVALID_SESSION_ID|invalid_grant|JwtGrantError|Client ID is required|Invalid SFDX auth URL|user hasn't approved this consumer|INVALID_LOGIN)
patterns.title: The pipeline cannot authenticate to the org
patterns.advice: Renew the auth URL or JWT secret. Check whether the deployment user is active, the password did not expire and the connected app still allows the user.

patterns.pattern: (?:ECONNRESET|ETIMEDOUT|ENOTFOUND|socket hang up|The client has timed out|UNKNOWN_EXCEPTION|Metadata API request failed|503 Service Unavailable|maintenance)
patterns.title: Network, timeout or platform problem
patterns.advice: Not caused by the change. Re-run. If the deployment itself timed out, raise the wait time; the deployment may still be running in the org.
